title: Time-lapse and cleared imaging of mouse embryonic lung explants to study three-dimensional cell morphology and topology dynamics
protocol: Euthanize mice humanely prior to embryo collection.
Dissect mouse lung rudiments from animals homozygous for Rosa26mTmG and heterozygous for ShhGFPCre allele.
Maintain dissected tissue in buffer between 20°C and 25°C to prevent drying and preserve morphology.
Wash freshly dissected lung rudiments clean in DPBS.
Submerge the tissue completely in culture/imaging medium.
Place submerged tissue in a humidified incubator set to 37°C and 5% CO2.
Allow tissue to rest for at least 1 hour before use.
Completely submerge fresh embryonic mouse explants in 4% PFA (∼ pH 7) in 1× PBS for 12–24 hours at 4°C.
Rinse tissues with PBS three times for at least 15 minutes each at 20°C–25°C on a rocking platform shaker.
Completely immerse the tissue in 5–7 mL of ½ CUBIC-1 solution.
Place the immersed tissue on a rocking platform shaker (30–60 RPM) at a temperature around 37°C for at least 2 days, changing the solution every 12–24 hours.
Discard ½-diluted CUBIC-1 solution.
Add 5–7 mL of undiluted CUBIC-1 solution immediately after discarding the previous solution.
Continue gentle shaking or rotation at 37°C for a minimum of 1 day, changing the solution every 12–24 hours until tissue is no longer cloudy or desired transparency is achieved.
Discard CUBIC-1 once transparency plateau is reached.
Rinse tissue with 15 mL of PBS three times for at least 4 hours each at 20°C–25°C to remove remaining CUBIC-1 completely.
Rotate explants when refreshing the CUBIC-1 solution to ensure uniform clearing results.
Minimize contact between explants and air, avoiding vigorous movements that introduce bubbles.
Wash samples serially with PBS.
Block samples with 5% BSA on a shaking platform at 4°C for 2-3 hours.
Incubate samples with primary antibodies in diluted 5% BSA on a rocking platform shaker at 4°C for 24 hours.
Rinse samples three times with 15 ml PBS for one hour each at 20-25°C.
Apply matching secondary antibodies to the sample under the same conditions as the primary incubations.
Rinse treated tissues three times with 15 ml PBS for at least one hour each at 20-25°C.
Discard half-diluted CUBIC-2 solution.
Add 5–7 mL of undiluted CUBIC-2 solution immediately.
Continue gentle shaking or rotation at 20°C–25°C for a minimum of 1 day.
Change the solution every 12–24 hours until desired transparency is achieved.
Ensure explants are entirely submerged and do not float.
Rotate explants when refreshing the CUBIC-2 solution.
Minimize explant contact with air or vigorous movements.
Degas the solution before use.
Handle treated tissues with care due to softness.
Adjust clearing regimens based on tissue composition for uniform results.
Pause point: Tissues may be kept in CUBIC-2 solution at 20°C–25°C for up to 1 year if necessary.
Melt a 4 mL aliquot of 2% low-melting point agarose mix in ddH2O in a heating block set to 70°C.
Keep the aliquot between 38°C-40°C to ensure it is close to gelling before embedding.
Transfer an E12.5 lung explant into the 38°C-40°C molten agarose mix.
Swirl the sample within the agarose mix carefully to ensure no surrounding film remains and the mix is homogeneous.
Select a glass capillary tube of 20 μL and a matching plunger rod.
Push the plunger through so the rod tip reaches the bottom of the capillary.
Insert the capillary tube into the agarose mix and slowly draw a single explant inside by pulling up the plunger, creating suction.
Orient the sample lengthwise as it enters the capillary.
Ensure there are ± 3 cm of free agarose above the explant and ±1 cm below it.
Cover seeded capillaries horizontally at 20°C–25°C until the agarose solidifies (approx. 15–20 minutes).
Rotate the covered capillaries halfway to ensure the explant is centered within the solidified agarose.
Punch a hole through the closed lid and bottom of a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube using tweezers.
Wriggle the seeded capillary through the perforated microcentrifuge tube.
Insert the microcentrifuge tube containing the capillary into a round-bottom glass centrifuge tube filled halfway with undiluted CUBIC-2 clearing solution.
Wrap parafilm tape around the microcentrifuge tube if necessary to ensure a tighter fit against the rim of the centrifuge tube.
Push the plunger rod down carefully to expose the bottom of the agarose column, ensuring the agarose-embedded sample is fully submerged in the CUBIC-2 clearing solution.
Place the centrifuge tube in a rack and cover it.
Allow the agarose to clear for a minimum of 1 day until the exposed agarose is no longer opaque.
Fill the imaging chamber slowly with CUBIC-2 clearing solution to avoid introducing bubbles.
Rest the sample undisturbed at 20°C–25°C for at least 1 h before imaging.
Avoid vigorous movements when fastening the capillary tube to the stage holder.
Work in sterile conditions when preparing hollow agarose cylinders.
Perform all steps under a laminar flow hood.
Plate standard culture/imaging medium in a rectangular 4-well dish.
Keep the plate in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Place a 4 mL aliquot of 2% low-melting point agarose mix in ddH2O in a heating block set to 70°C.
Melt the agarose and keep it in a second heating block or heated shaker between 38°C–40°C.
Cut the end of a P200 non-filtered pipette tip with a scalpel, then insert a 20 μL glass capillary tube through the cut end by pushing the matching plunger rod until its tip reaches the bottom.
Cut an FEP tube segment measuring approximately 2.5 cm.
Attach the cut FEP tube segment to the cut end of the P200 pipette tip encasing the capillary tube.
Ensure the capillary tube is centered and spans no more than 60% of the total length, with a free distance of 2-3 mm from the sides of the FEP tube.
Hold the assembly upside-down and slowly pour approximately 300 μl of molten agarose into the open tube end.
Rest the assembly horizontally at 4°C until the agarose solidifies (approximately 15-20 minutes).
Slowly rotate the capillary within the FEP to detach from the agarose.
Carefully remove the pipette tip and set it aside.
Flip over and gently push the capillary while holding onto the FEP tube to dislodge the agarose cylinder.
Using tweezers, slide away the agarose cylinder into the culture/imaging medium within the prepared 4-well dish.
Equilibrate immersed hollow cylinders in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Fill a glass vial with culture/imaging medium halfway and keep it in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Pour a 100 μL droplet of undiluted Matrigel into a petri dish.
Transfer a rested lung explant using a glass capillary, ensuring to carry over as little culture/imaging medium as possible.
Pour 200 μL of undiluted Matrigel into the same petri dish and carefully swirl to fully embed the sample.
Insert a glass capillary (20 μL volume) and slowly draw in the explant and Matrigel, ensuring the sample is orientated lengthwise and avoiding any bubbles around the sample.
Transfer the sample and Matrigel mixture into an equilibrated hollow agarose cylinder by slowly pushing down the plunger while using forceps to keep the cylinder upright.
Lay the cylinder horizontally in the plate with warm media and lightly rotate until the Matrigel polymerizes.
Ensure that the explant is surrounded by Matrigel and does not contact the inner radius of the hollow agarose cylinder.
Hold the seeded agarose cylinder at a 30-degree angle using forceps.
Gently reinsert the glass capillary, plunger rod, and pipette tip into the opening of the seeded agarose cylinder.
Insert the capillary holding the agarose cylinder into a glass vial with warm medium.
Place the pipette tip on the lid of the glass vial to ensure that the capillary is adequately submerged in the medium without touching the bottom.
Transfer the glass vial containing the agarose cylinder and medium into a humidified incubator.
Equilibrate the sample for 1 hour at 37°C and 5% CO2 before imaging.
Ultrasonicate the imaging chamber at 80°C for at least 20 minutes.
Rinse the ultrasonicated imaging chamber with 70% ethanol and sterile PBS.
Fill the imaging chamber with culture/imaging medium.
Allow the system to equilibrate undisturbed at 37°C with 5% CO2 for at least 2 hours before mounting a hollow agarose cylinder.
Supply 0.4 ml of culture medium per hour using two peristaltic pumps.
Extract 0.2 ml of culture medium per hour to maintain a fresh environment.
Fill the imaging chamber slowly to avoid frothing.
